newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Shell to raise investment in E&P.
newsitem.headline: Shell to raise investment in E&P.

text.p: Royal Dutch/Shell said on Thursday it would steadily increase the share of its business devoted to exploration and production (E &P), partly at the expense of its refining and marketing activities.

"Over a period of five years we plan to invest $64 billion and the share of exploration and production (in the group) will rise from 50 percent to 57 percent. The refinery side will decline from 36 percent to 26 percent," Shell co-chairman Cor Herkstroeter told a news conference in the Hague.
"In the years to come we will spend even more in exploration and production," he said.
The expenditure was expected to result in the growth of its natural gas and oil production of seven percent a year from now until 2001, the company said.
Herkstroeter also emphasised that healthy profits from exploration and production were not simply the result of higher oil prices. Cost reductions were more important, he said.

"The higher oil prices did make a contribution to profits. But in the fourth quarter, exploration and production performed 93 percent better (than a year ago), while the oil price was only 39 percent higher," he said.
He was not prepared to predict the price of oil for 1997.
Full year profit from exploration and production totalled 3.16 billion sterling against 1.92 billion sterling in 1995, a rise of 65 percent.
